the iranian government—the hardliners included—have every reason to engage in talks with the united states that extends the ceasefire. 

implementing an agreement is another matter.

even finland president alex stubb—one of the strongest pro-american leaders in europe today—expressing his unhappiness with what he considers trump’s america alone policies of late.

viktor orbán has been decisively voted out of power, losing to péter maygar.
this wasn’t a shift to the left, it was a rejection of kleptocracy. linkedin.com/posts/ianbremme…

imf and world bank resume relations with venezuela.

the economy will substantially improve. the politics a different question.

the outlines of a us-iran deal are taking shape/getting closer. 

the us wants iran's enriched uranium stockpile and a 20-year moratorium on enrichment. iran is offering stockpile plus 5 years, wants $20 billion in frozen funds released plus sanctions relief.
iran declares strait of hormuz open to commercial traffic  — for the duration of the israel-lebanon ceasefire.

iea: this is the largest energy crisis we have ever faced.

europe: ~6 weeks of jet fuel. flight cancellations coming.

developing countries in asia, africa, latin america: already hit harder, heard less.

leaders aren’t giving trump unvarnished, real expertise or advice, and it’s not just happening among members the administration and business leaders.
it’s happening with world leaders too.

trump much more capable of ending an israel war (in lebanon) than netanyahu was of starting an american one (in iran).

xi and trump make an iran breakthrough!

$2t → $2.7t in 6 years. and that's before the iran war, before europe's (and asia's) defense spending push, before the $90b ukraine loan.

the chart from 2026 is going to look even steeper.

the conventional wisdom was that a destabilizing war in the oil-producing heart of the middle east would badly hurt china.
it hasn’t worked out that way. so far, china is weathering the war with iran better than many of its neighbors and looks set to emerge stronger. gzeromedia.com/by-ian-bremme…

netanyahu survived oct. 7 and engineered one of the greatest political comebacks of the era. he hasn't resolved the central tension: what saved him politically may destroy israel's standing internationally. time.com/collection/100-most…

24% of americans think the iran war has been worth the costs and benefits. 35% approve of the military strikes. even among republicans, just 55% say it's been worth it.

nearly half of trump's own party either opposed or uncertain about his signature foreign policy action.

the s&p 500 has fully recovered to pre-iran war levels. the strait of hormuz is still effectively closed, disrupting global supply chains. oil is still near $100. inflation just hit a three-year high. the market has decided none of that matters. ai doing a lot of lifting here.

the us is sending 10,000+ more troops to the middle east while simultaneously pursuing ceasefire talks in islamabad. trump clearly wants to announce a quick win and deescalate. but worth remembering that the pentagon is preparing for "the possibility of additional strikes or ground operations."

trump declaring victory in war with iran and deescalating is by far the smartest move he can make right now. 

would’ve been better weeks ago. but it’s welcome nonetheless.
